subject: Lifeboat: one-time credit + term reset request for Renewal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Lifeboat: one-time credit + term reset request for Renewal

Team —

Quick summary: Lifeboat (current ARR $340k) is up for renewal on 6/15. They are threatening to move to a competitor unless we provide a tailored retention package. Customer is strategic: embedded in three product lines and in active pilots with potential to expand to an enterprise suite next year.

What I’m asking for: executive approval to offer a one-time retention package that combines: 
- 25% off list for year 1 only (applied to committed seats)
- $200,000 one-time account credit to offset migration costs (applied as invoice credit)
- Term reset: move from remaining 12 months to a 24-month renewed commitment
- SLA addendum: 99.9% availability + 4-hour P1 response window for the first 6 months (with measurable credits)

Rationale: without this, customer has signaled an imminent PO to a competitor. The account has consistent usage growth (see HubSpot notes) and two upcoming pilots that likely convert to +$600k ARR in 12–18 months if we keep them. We have limited leverage on price but strong operational differentiation (latency, support).

Risk/controls: 
- Offer is one-time and explicitly applies to renewal signature only.
- Credit is non-refundable and amortized over renewal invoices; legal redline attached.
- I propose we cap discount to committed seats only and include a 10% early termination recoup if they break the new 24-mo term in year 1.

Attachments: Lifeboat_Proposal_v3.pdf (proposal + pricing), Lifeboat_SLA_Addendum_redline.docx

Next step: Need yes/no on the package (or alternate dollar cap). If approved, I’ll get Legal to send the DocuSign and Procurement to confirm timeline. They want an answer by 5/18 EOD.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-16T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lifeboat: one-time credit + term reset request for Renewal

Karthik —

Thanks for the concise ask. Two quick questions before I can green-light: 
1) Impact to 2028 ARR and gross margin (please show the delta with and without the credit).
2) Confirm customer expansion probability and timing for the pilots you mentioned (are these contractually committed or best-effort?).

Marissa — can you run a quick margin / P&L on this? I want to see the net NPV over 24 months. If numbers look acceptable, I’m inclined to approve with legal safeguards.

Vivek
SVP, Sales Operations

Date: 2028-05-17T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lifeboat: one-time credit + term reset request for Renewal

Vivek / Karthik —

I ran preliminary numbers. Notes below: 
- If we apply 25% off year 1 + $200k credit, 2028 recognized revenue drops ~ $170k on a cash basis but NPV over 24 months (assuming expansion to +$600k in year 2) could still be positive; need to validate conversion probability.
- Biggest concern: heavy front-loaded concession with little contractual protection if they churn after year 1. The early termination recoup you mentioned is necessary.

Recommended contract language to protect us (suggested Legal redlines in attached SLA addendum): 
- Amortize the $200k credit over 12 invoices and require repayment pro-rata if they terminate before 12 months.
- Limit discount to named seats + explicit cap on added usage at full price.
- Add milestone-based pilot conversion language: we should require signed statement of intent or mutually agreed acceptance criteria for pilots that trigger conversion discounts.

If we get those in writing and can amortize credit, I’m okay to recommend approval. We should still limit to one-time approval and require a deal desk sign-off threshold (e.g., >$150k credit requires VP sign-off).

Marissa
Head of Finance, Commercial

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-17T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lifeboat: one-time credit + term reset request for Renewal

Quick follow-up — answers inline and rationale: 

Vivek Q1 (impact): 
- Worst-case 2028 recognized revenue delta = -$170,000 (cash), net NPV over 24 months ~ +$240,000 assuming 60% chance of pilot conversion to paid seats in H1 2029. I attached a simple model in the Drive link.

Vivek Q2 (pilot status): 
- Two pilots are contractor-led (not yet contractually committed). We have written evaluation plans and a customer PO intent emailed by Jordan on 2028-04-11 (I’ll forward). I will make pilot acceptance criteria part of the contract as Marissa suggested.

Mitigations I propose (to address finance/legal concerns): 
- Convert $200k credit to an amortized credit across 12 monthly invoices with pro-rata repayment on early termination.
- Discount applies only to 150 named seats (explicit roster attached).
- Add a one-time 10% recoupment fee if they terminate within 12 months of the renewal signature.
- Include SLA addendum redline that ties credits to verifiable uptime metrics (see redline attached).

Customer asks to close by 5/18 EOD. If we wait longer, they begin procurement with competitor. I’m recommending approval with the mitigations above.

Karthik

Subject: FWD: Lifeboat: one-time credit + term reset request for Renewal — Exec approval needed by 5/18 EOD

Aditya —

Looping you in for executive sign-off. Karthik and Marissa have a mitigated structure: 
- 25% off list year 1 (committed seats only)
- $200k amortized credit (12 months, pro-rata repayment on early termination)
- 24-month term reset 
- SLA addendum (99.9% + 4-hour P1 response) with financial credits limited and conditioned on monitoring data

I recommend we approve this one-time package to prevent churn; financial exposure appears controlled with amortization and recoupment clauses. Customer requires final confirmation by COB today.

If you approve, please reply all with "APPROVED" and I’ll trigger Legal for DocuSign. If you prefer a cap, suggest a maximum net concession of $220k.

Vivek
SVP, Sales Operations
